en: For over a thousand years, the western European world has falsely denied the Romanness of the eastern empire and its majority population. Prejudice and polemic were piled on top of the original sin of denialism in an orgy of contempt that lasted well into the twentieth century. The eastern Romans were viewed as effeminate “Greeks,” then as schismatics and heretics, as degenerate Christians, servile subjects of an oriental theocratic despotism, and the source of Soviet oppression. The “Greek” label was a fundamental distortion of east Roman culture, but it nevertheless preserved the idea that it represented a nation. Even that was lost, however, in the later nineteenth century due to the imperial anxieties of the Great Powers. When Byzantine Studies emerged as a professional academic discipline, the field retreated from the politically charged “Greek” label and fully embraced the empty abstraction of “Byzantium,” whose majority population was seen as lacking ethnicity and nationality. The “Byzantines” were henceforth defined by their faith, Orthodoxy, which therefore drew the lion’s share of both scholarly and popular attention during the twentieth century. The unambiguous evidence of the sources for the polity of the Romans was disregarded, a feat of intellectual discipline that can be accomplished only after years of graduate training. The national basis of Romanía was marginalized in favor of theological abstractions lifted from the writings of a few bishops, such as Eusebios of Kaisareia.
zh: 一千多年来，西欧世界一直错误地否认东部帝国及其多数人口的罗马性。从这项否认的原罪出发，偏见和论战层层累积，掀起一场蔑视的狂欢，进入二十世纪后还延续了很久。东罗马人先被视作阴柔的“希腊人”，后来又成了分裂派、异端、堕落的基督徒、臣服于东方神权专制的人，乃至苏维埃压迫的源头。称他们为“希腊人”，从根本上歪曲了东罗马文化，却还承认这种文化代表着一个民族。到十九世纪后期，列强出于各自的帝国处境而心存戒惧，连这点也丢掉了。拜占庭研究兴起为一门专业学科后，便撇开政治意味浓厚的“希腊”标签，全盘接受了“拜占庭”这个空洞的抽象概念，并认为其多数居民既无族群也无民族归属。从此，人们以正教信仰界定“拜占庭人”。到了二十世纪，拜占庭领域的学者和公众也就把大部分注意力放在了正教上。史料明白记载罗马人的政治共同体，却遭到无视。没有多年研究生训练，很难练就这番学术定力。罗曼尼亚的民族基础被置于边缘，取而代之的是从凯撒利亚的欧塞比乌斯等少数主教著作中提炼出来的神学抽象。

en: At the same time, the existence of minority ethnic groups in the empire, urged by modern national states and their historians, was taken at face value. The result was a monstrously inverted riddle, the only “empire” in history about which it was possible to identify ethnic minorities but not the majority. More than that, it became unclear whether this was an empire or some other kind of state. Were there ruling and ruled ethnic groups specific enough to be named, or only a deracinated Orthodox “elite” that ruled over a majority with no name and various minorities that could be named if only they enjoyed the advantage of modern national spokesmen? Were “the Byzantines” the ones ruling this state, and were they the ones who are called “Romans” in the sources? Or were all of the empire’s subjects “Byzantines,” both those who “called themselves Romans” and the rest? Could minorities exist with no majority?
zh: 与此同时，帝国内有哪些少数族群，现代民族国家及其史家怎么说，学界便怎么信。结果是一个荒谬颠倒的谜：历史上唯一一个能识别出少数族群、却识别不出多数族群的“帝国”。更有甚者，这究竟是一个帝国还是别的某种国家，也变得不清楚了。可否说出哪些族群统治、哪些族群被统治？还是说，这里只有一批没有族群根基的正教“精英”，统治着无名的多数人和若干少数群体，而后者仅因有现代民族替他们发声才叫得出名字？“拜占庭人”是统治这个国家的人吗？他们就是史料中被称为“罗马人”的那些人吗？抑或帝国所有臣民都是“拜占庭人”，既包括那些“自称罗马人”者，也包括其余人？没有多数，少数能存在吗？

en: Such were the confusions that resulted when the empirical commitments of scholarship yielded to the ideological commitments of denialism. As a result, our books are full of baffling statements. Consider, for example, the claim that a Greek identity and the Greek language were not requirements for anyone to be considered a Byzantine.

What is this trying to say, if we were to translate it from the invented terminology of modern scholarship into real-world terms? That one did not have to be a Roman to be a subject of the emperor? But isn’t that merely to say that the Romans had an empire? This is true but also redundant, because there were never any requirements for being the subject of an empire. The field of Byzantine Studies, tangled up in the terminological weeds that it itself has sown, has operated in this state of cognitive dissonance for over a century. Its scholars read the name “Roman” in the sources, but many of them cannot “see” it. The goal of this book has been to make it harder to unsee.
zh: 学界一旦为了坚持意识形态上的否认而放弃由证据说话，就会出现这类混乱。结果，我们的书里充满了令人困惑的陈述。例如，考虑这样一种说法：一个人无须具备希腊身份或讲希腊语，也可以被视为拜占庭人。
如果我们把它从现代学术生造的术语翻译成现实世界的说法，这究竟想说什么？是说一个人不必是罗马人也能做皇帝的臣民？但这岂不只是说罗马人拥有一个帝国？这话不错，却也多余，因为成为帝国的臣民本来就没有这类资格要求。一个多世纪以来，拜占庭研究一直被自己的术语缠住，走不出这种认知失调。它的学者们在史料中读到“罗马人”这个称谓，其中许多人却“看”不见它。本书的目标，就是让人更难对它视而不见。

en: To remove this blockage and understand Byzantium as an empire, we have to take the evidence of our sources regarding ethnicity seriously. This requires that we remove the edifices of denial that have been built up to block our view.
zh: 要清除这一阻碍、把拜占庭理解为一个帝国，我们必须认真看待史料中关于族群身份的证据。这就要拆掉那层层搭起、遮挡视线的否认论。

en: As the evidence piles up, the dissonance can mount until it becomes too much to bear and the opinion topples over, a phenomenon called the affective tipping point. The tipping point depends on the balance between how badly the opinion holder’s reputation would de damaged by relinquishing the opinion and whether the counterevidence is so blatant and public as to be common knowledge: a naked emperor, an elephant in the room.
zh: 随着证据不断累积，认知失调也会愈演愈烈，直至让人无从承受，原有观点随之垮掉，这一现象被称为情感临界点。何时越过临界点，取决于放弃原有观点会使持有者的声誉受损到什么程度，也取决于反证是否已公然摆在眼前、到了人人皆知的地步：一个没穿衣服的皇帝，房间里的一头大象。

en: The evidence is extensive and incontrovertible. What we call Byzantium was a Roman polity populated overwhelmingly by identifiable ethnic Romans and a number of ethnic minorities. “Roman” was not an elite court identity or a literary affect: it was a nationality that extended to most of the population regardless of its location, occupation, gender, and class (i.e., roughly to all who were Greek-speaking and Orthodox). It was common Romans who began to call their land and state
“Romanland,” and to call their language

They had a reasonably clear awareness of who in their state were not Romans. The size of these ethnic minorities was usually quite small (e.g., in the early tenth century), although it grew in phases of imperial expansion (in the late tenth and early eleventh centuries). Therefore, for most of its history in this period, the Roman state was not much of an “empire.” Even in those phases, the size of unassimilated ethnic minorities was probably not so great in relation to the Roman population that it necessarily tilted the balance toward “empire” as the primary category that we should be using. To be sure, historians have not found a minimum threshold ratio of ethnic diversity for a state to qualify as an empire, nor have they sought one. But generally speaking Byzantium usually lay closer to the national state end of the spectrum (as Romanía), though it made occasional forays in a more imperial direction (as the hegemony of the Romans over others).
zh: 证据充分而无可辩驳。我们所谓的拜占庭，是一个罗马政治共同体，绝大多数人口都可辨明为族群意义上的罗马人，另有若干少数族群。“罗马”不是一种精英宫廷身份或文学矫饰：它是一种遍及多数人口的民族身份，跨越地域、职业、性别与阶级（大致涵盖讲希腊语且信奉正教的人）。正是普通罗马人开始把他们的土地和国家称为
（罗曼尼亚），即“罗马之地”，把他们的语言称为

（罗马语）。他们相当清楚地意识到自己国家里哪些人不是罗马人。这些少数族群的规模通常很小（例如十世纪早期），尽管在帝国扩张阶段有所增长（十世纪后期和十一世纪早期）。因此，在这一时期的大部分历史中，罗马国家算不上什么“帝国”。即使在扩张阶段，未被同化的少数族群和罗马人口相比，比例恐怕也没有大到非把“帝国”作为首要范畴来理解这个国家不可。诚然，历史学家尚未找到一个具体的人口比例，用来判定国家的族群多样性达到什么程度才能称为帝国，也没有尝试找出这样的比例。但总体而言，在民族国家和帝国之间，拜占庭通常更偏向民族国家的一端，即罗曼尼亚；有时罗马人也对其他族群实行统治，向帝国的一端靠拢。

en: All states, including nation-states, are multiethnic. The standard for empire is found in the regimes of difference by which nonruling groups are governed. In Romanía, there is evidence for assimilation and inclusion as well as for intolerance, persecution, second-class citizenship, guest-elite status, grudging toleration, and differential access to power. Now that we have a working model of ethnicity and empire we can begin to write the history of Byzantium along these lines, as historians have long been doing for other empires. But to study the management of difference, we have to first be able to “see” the ethnoreligious distinctions on which it was based. This, in turn, requires that we recognize the Romans as a group distinct from the rest, as in fact they are consistently presented in all the sources, both Byzantine and foreign.
zh: 所有国家，包括民族国家，都是多族群的。判断一个国家是不是帝国，要看它是否通过区别对待的制度来治理那些不掌权的群体。在罗曼尼亚，既有同化与包容的证据，也有不宽容、迫害、二等公民身份、外来精英的地位、勉强容忍以及获取权力的机会不均的证据。既然我们已有了一个分析族群和帝国的框架，就可以开始沿这些线索书写拜占庭的历史，正如历史学家长期以来对其他帝国所做的那样。但要研究差异的管理，我们首先必须能够“看见”它所依据的族群和宗教界限。这反过来又要求我们承认罗马人是一个有别于其余人的群体，正如所有史料——拜占庭的和外国的——事实上都一贯呈现的那样。

en: It also requires that we discard notions of immutable ethnicity, or race, which retain a hold on Byzantine Studies due to the claims pressed by nationalist schools of historiography and the field’s own unreconstructed view of ethnicity, which predates the mid-twentieth century. In most fields of research since then, ethnicity is understood as mutable, as a cultural artifact produced by societal change, not something that inheres in biologically defined groups. Historians of Byzantium in particular have to accept this approach for two reasons. First, ever since antiquity foreign groups and individuals who entered the empire could assimilate and become Roman, discarding their former identities or retaining only symbolic traces of them. Romanness was a cultural-political identity that could on occasion represent itself through largely symbolic narratives of shared ancestry. By assimilating to its institutions, foreigners could make themselves part of those narratives of belonging. And second, the very existence of Romanía itself was the product of ethnic change among the eastern subjects of the ancient Roman empire. It emerged from specific processes at a particular time in history, and likewise later disappeared. There are now no more eastern Romans. But that does not authorize us to deny that they ever existed.
zh: 这也要求放弃族群或种族一成不变的看法。民族主义史学诸派一力主张这一点，拜占庭研究本身也一直沿用二十世纪中叶以前的族群观，两者使这种观念至今仍有影响。自那以后，在大多数研究领域，族群性被理解为可变的，是社会变迁所造就的文化产物，而非某种内在于生物学界定群体的东西。拜占庭历史学家尤其必须接受这一取径，理由有二。第一，自古以来，进入帝国的外国群体和个人都能够同化并成为罗马人，抛弃其原有身份，或只保留其象征性痕迹。罗马性是一种文化政治身份，有时用共同祖先的故事来表现自身，而这些故事主要起象征作用。外来者融入罗马制度之后，自己也可以加入这些界定归属的叙事。第二，罗曼尼亚本身的存在，正是古代罗马帝国东部臣民之间族群变迁的产物。它在特定的历史条件下逐渐形成，后来也同样逐渐消失。如今已没有东罗马人，我们却不能因此否认他们曾经存在过。

en: At the same time, I would caution against the extreme use of “fluidity” for studying ethnicity. In fields that have accepted the paradigm of ethnic change, it has become fashionable in some quarters to treat ethnicity as infinitely malleable, negotiated and renegotiated on a daily or instantaneous basis, and ultimately as an evanescent or unreal social artifact. One can allegedly wake up in a Serbian household, play the Greek in the marketplace in the morning, then switch to an Albanian persona at a wedding in the evening, pray at a Muslim shrine, and correspond with Jewish relatives at night. I suspect that such models reflect the ideals and hopes of late modern liberalism and are inherently political. They are a misleading and even fictional basis for studying historical ethnicities, which are not that easy to perform in a native way. Most people can manage only one in a convincing way, two at most. Truly “fluid” people are extremely rare. Moreover, ethnicities are social and not individual constructs, and, if they survive for a significant period, are deeply grounded in the maintenance among a large group of narratives, institutions, and specific markers such as language. These are hard to change. It can happen, but it takes time, effort, powerful incentives, or a dramatic change of circumstances. If we must use the metaphor, the “fluid” in question is more like honey, tar, or glue, and less like water or blood. If you doubt this, go to any group with a fairly well-defined identity and try to change its narrative about itself.
zh: 与此同时，我也要提醒，研究族群时，不宜把“流动性”推到极端。在已经接受族群会变化的研究领域，有些人习惯将族群身份看成可以任意改变，每天甚至每时每刻都能靠协商重新确定，最终当作一种转瞬即逝或不真实的社会产物。据说一个人可以在塞尔维亚家庭里醒来，早上在市场扮演希腊人，晚上在婚礼上切换到阿尔巴尼亚身份，在穆斯林圣所祈祷，夜里与犹太亲戚通信。我怀疑这类模型反映的是晚期现代自由主义的理想与希望，本质上带有政治性。用这样的模型来研究历史上的族群容易产生误解，甚至有如从虚构出发，因为要表现得像一个群体的土生成员，并非易事。大多数人只能令人信服地表现出一种族群身份，至多两种。真正“流动”的人极其罕见。此外，族群性是社会建构而非个人建构，能长期存续的族群，都有大批成员维系它的叙事、制度以及语言等独特标志。这些很难改变。改变可以发生，但需要时间、努力、强大的激励，或境况的剧变。如果我们非用这个隐喻不可，那么这里所谓的“流体”更像蜂蜜、焦油或胶水，而不像水或血。你若不信，就去任何一个认同界定相当清晰的群体，试着改变它关于自身的叙事。

en: The Romans of Byzantium did come into being and did go extinct, but both events were processes that lasted for centuries and were precipitated by conquest, incentives, and dramatic historical change on either end. In between, however, they kept their Romanness together for over a thousand years through the maintenances of their narratives, institutions, and specific culture. Now, a group of this size that names its homeland, state, language, common culture, and monarch after itself is what we call a nation. This has significant implications.
zh: 拜占庭的罗马人确实形成过，也确实消亡了。形成和消亡都历经数百年，都因征服、利益驱动以及剧烈的历史变迁而加速。在其间的一千多年里，他们靠维系自身的叙事、制度和特有文化，共同保存了罗马性。这么大一个群体，以自身之名来称呼家园、国家、语言、共同文化乃至君主，这就是我们所谓的民族。承认这一点意义重大。

en: One set of implications has to do with Byzantine history as a national narrative. Consider, for example, the reaction of the Romans to the loss of their capital in 1204 and the dismemberment of their polity. That reaction in all ways refutes the attenuated and anemic versions of Roman identity served up by the denialist tradition, while conversely it exactly matches what we would expect of an ethnic group deprived through aggression of its national state. The language of ethnic and even racial difference between Romans and others is pervasive in this period. Moreover, the Romans could recognize each other across the lines of the different and competing states that they set up in the aftermath of 1204: they knew who was Roman, independent of statehood. They were, moreover, insistent on reclaiming and restoring their lost homeland, by which they meant more than just Constantinople. Also, they did not have an “Orthodox” state in mind, as the Bulgarians and Vlachs were among their major opponents. All these elements of ethnicity did not suddenly appear out of nowhere in 1204. They had been there all along and were only amplified now by outrage and loss.
zh: 首先，这关系到怎样把拜占庭史写成一部民族史。试看1204年失去都城、政治共同体遭到肢解之后罗马人的反应。这些反应完全不同于否认论所描绘的淡薄无力的罗马身份，却正如一个因入侵而丧失民族国家的族群所会有的反应。罗马人与其他人之间族群乃至种族差异的话语，在这一时期无处不在。此外，罗马人能够跨越1204年之后各个相互竞争的罗马政权的疆界，彼此认出对方：他们知道谁是罗马人，与国家归属无关。而且，他们坚持收复与重建失去的家园，其所指不只是君士坦丁堡。还有，他们心中并没有一个“正教”国家，因为保加尔人和弗拉赫人就在他们的主要对手之列。这些族群认同的要素早已存在，只是1204年后的愤怒和失去家园的经历使它们显得更为鲜明。

en: The second set of implications is more theoretical and points to a need for more research on the formation and subsistence of premodern national states. Many historians are slowly but surely rejecting the modernist doctrine, which avers that only modern developments (e.g., telegraphs, newspapers, industry, and universal schooling) can create nation-states. I intend to situate Romanía within the growing rejection of this doctrine in a separate book, which will focus, beyond ethnicity, on institutions and governmentality. Yet it is still common to read that “cultural homogeneity of the kind the modern nation-state produced was beyond the reach of even the most infrastructurally developed of these ancient states.” The concern is with “technological constraints,” even though the footnote then refers to the “remarkably complex and efficient communicative apparatuses [that] ancient empires developed.”
zh: 其次，在理论上，这也引出一个有待进一步研究的问题，即前现代民族国家如何形成并存续。许多历史学家正逐步放弃现代主义的教条，即只有现代条件（如电报、报纸、工业和普及教育）才能造就民族国家。我打算另写一部书，从这种日益受到认同的批判立场出发考察罗曼尼亚。除族群问题外，那部书还将着重讨论制度与治理术。然而，人们仍常读到这样的说法：“现代民族国家所造就的那种文化同质性，即便是这些古代国家中基础设施最发达者也无法企及。”其关注点在于“技术约束”，尽管脚注随后又提到“古代帝国发展出了异常复杂而高效的信息传递体系”。

en: This reasoning places the cart before the horse. Cultural homogeneity is one of the most striking features of Byzantine society. Rather than denying it on dubious a priori grounds, we should instead be searching for the mechanisms—both the institutions and processes—that created and sustained it. Consider the following double standard. The same scholars who might deny that premodern means created cultural homogeneity on a national level, and who also deny that the Byzantines were Romans, will at the same time readily admit—even insist—that Byzantine society was thoroughly Christianized, indeed that Christianity had created radically new subjectivities and through these reshaped the entire population on a deep personal level. But if the “means” existed for the one transformation, they existed for the other. The two were not so different. Both created identities associated with specific labels that entailed distinctive beliefs about one’s place in the world and one’s relations with others; constitutive practices; and public and private performative scripts. Why do we believe that the ancient world could spread a religious belief that reformatted people “all the way down,” both socially and personally, but that the same could not be done with their political and ethnic identities? The same argument can be made for Islamization and Arabization in the eastern provinces after the seventh century. Those were also deep and broad developments that changed ethnicities, beliefs, practices, narratives, and languages for the majority. This too happened, and institutions played a key role in promoting them.
zh: 这种推理本末倒置。文化同质性是拜占庭社会最显著的特征之一。我们不应基于可疑的先验理由否认它，而应转而探寻创造并维系它的机制——包括制度与过程。考虑下面这种双重标准。同样那些学者，可能否认前现代手段在民族层面创造了文化同质性，也否认拜占庭人是罗马人，却同时会欣然承认——甚至坚持——拜占庭社会已彻底基督教化，的确，基督教甚至造就了全新的主体性，并借此深刻改变了社会中每个个体理解自身的方式。但是，如果一种转变的“手段”存在，那么另一种转变的手段也存在。两者并无太大不同。两种转变都带来了以特定名称标识的身份。与这些身份相伴的，是对自己在世界中的位置以及与他人关系的特定看法、构成这种身份的实践，以及在公共和私人场合表现这一身份的行为方式。既然我们相信古代世界可以传播一种宗教信仰，从社会到个人“彻底”重塑人，为什么不相信政治与族群身份也能由类似的过程形成？同样的论证也适用于七世纪之后东部行省的伊斯兰化与阿拉伯化。这种广泛而深刻的变化同样改变了多数人的族群身份、信仰、实践、叙事和语言，而制度在其中起了关键作用。

en: It remains then to show in detail how the institutions and public ideology of the state could create, sustain, reflect, or be enmeshed with the Romanness of the majority of its subjects. Through what mechanisms did Romanía constitute itself as a national state, and by what channels was governmentality disseminated? Were average Romans so oppressed by their own elites, as some believe, that there could be no meaningful community of interest between them, or was Romanía a state whose existence and extraordinary survival required the efforts and attachment of an entire people and not just the short-term ambitions of a narrow elite?
zh: 接下来，还须具体说明国家的制度与公共意识形态如何造就、维系和反映多数臣民的罗马性，又怎样可能与它交织在一起。罗曼尼亚通过什么机制把自身构建为一个民族国家，治理术又通过什么渠道推行？如一些人所想，普通罗马人是否受本国精英压迫太深，以至双方根本不存在任何实质性的共同利益？还是说，罗曼尼亚得以存在并存续如此之久，需要整个民族的努力和归属感，单凭少数精英的短期野心做不到？
